cues.text: We’ve got to choose a topic for our experiment, haven’t we, Jack? Were you thinking of something to do with seeds?
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: That’s right. I thought we could look at seed germination – how a seed begins to grow.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: OK. Any particular reason? I know you’re hoping to work in plant science eventually …
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Yeah, but practically everything we do is going to feed into that. No, there’s an optional module on seed structure and function in the third year that I might do, so I thought it might be useful for that. If I choose that option, I don’t have to do a dissertation module.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: Good idea.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Well, I thought for this experiment we could look at the relationship between seed size and the way the seeds are planted. So, we could plant different sized seeds in different ways, and see which grow best.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: OK. We’d need to allow time for the seeds to come up.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: That should be fine if we start now. A lot of the other possible experiments need quite a bit longer.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: So that’d make it a good one to choose. And I don’t suppose it’d need much equipment; we’re not doing chemical analysis or anything. Though that’s not really an issue, we’ve got plenty of equipment in the laboratory.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Yeah. We need to have a word with the tutor if we’re going to go ahead with it though. I’m sure our aim’s OK. It’s not very ambitious but the assignment’s only ten percent of our final mark, isn’t it? But we need to be sure we’re the only ones doing it
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: Yeah, it’s only five percent actually, but it’d be a bit boring if everyone was doing it.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Did you read that book on seed germination on our reading list?
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: The one by Graves? I looked through it for my last experiment, though it wasn’t all that relevant there. It would be for this experiment, though. I found it quite hard to follow – lots about the theory, which I hadn’t expected
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Yes, I’d been hoping for something more practical. It does include references to the recent findings on genetically-modified seeds, though.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: Yes, that was interesting.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: I read an article about seed germination by Lee Hall.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: About seeds that lie in the ground for ages and only germinate after a fire?
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: That’s the one. I knew a bit about it already, but not about this research. His analysis of figures comparing the times of the fires and the proportion of seeds that germinated was done in a lot of detail – very impressive
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: Was that the article with the illustrations of early stages of plant development? They were very clear.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: I think those diagrams were in another article.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: Anyway, shall we have a look at the procedure for our experiment? We’ll need to get going with it quite soon.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Right. So the first thing we have to do is find our seeds. I think vegetable seeds would be best. And obviously they mustn’t all be the same size. So, how many sorts do we need? About four different ones?
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: I think that would be enough. There’ll be quite a large number of seeds for each one.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Then, for each seed we need to find out how much it weighs, and also measure its dimensions, and we need to keep a careful record of all that.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: That’ll be quite time-consuming. And we also need to decide how deep we’re going to plant the seeds – right on the surface, a few millimetres down, or several centimetres.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: OK. So then we get planting. Do you think we can plant several seeds together in the same plant pot?
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: No, I think we need a different one for each seed.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: Right. And we’ll need to label them – we can use different coloured labels. Then we wait for the seeds to germinate – I reckon that’ll be about three weeks, depending on what the weather’s like. Then we see if our plants have come up, and write down how tall they’ve grown.
cues.speaker: JACK

cues.text: Then all we have to do is look at our numbers, and see if there’s any relation between them.
cues.speaker: EMMA

cues.text: That’s right. So …
cues.speaker: JACK
